title: Posterior Leg and Calf Region Massage
summary: Massage of the posterior leg and calf region from the knee to the ankle — with focus on tension points, knots, stress areas, and pain points.

sections.title: About This Region
paragraphs: The posterior leg and calf region runs from the knee to the ankle along the back of the leg. It includes the calf muscles and the structures that connect down toward the heel.
This area often holds deep muscle tension. Work carefully and thoroughly so the client leaves with real relief, not just a quick pass over the surface.

sections.title: What to Find and Release
paragraphs: As you massage, actively search for and release:
sections.closing: Spend extra time wherever you find tightness, knots, or discomfort. Do not rush past these areas.

sections.title: Timing Standard
paragraphs: Follow the approved timing unless tension, knots, or pain areas clearly need more care.
list: Four hands: 10 minutes for each leg.
Two hands: 13 minutes for each leg.
Spend extra time on muscle tension points, knots, stress areas, and pain points.

sections.title: You Are Not Done Until It Is Done
paragraphs: A posterior leg and calf region massage is complete only when the leg shows clear improvement — not when the clock runs out.
sections.closing: If the leg is still tight, knotted, or the client still feels tension, continue working — especially on tension points, knots, stress areas, and pain points — until the standard is met.
